item.title: [10] Interfacial polarity control of anomalous Hall effect in LaCoO3-SrIrO3 heterostructures
item.description:
Last authors: Sangjae Lee, Changyoung Kim

Authors: Yeonjae Lee, Chanyoung Shin, Youngdo Kim, et al.

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: author whitelist: Changyoung Kim

Tags: #angle-resolvedphotoemission #photoemission #anomalousHall #heterostructure #topological #Halleffect #transport

Abstract: Interfacial polarity in oxide heterostructures can drive robust charge redistribution across the interface, yet its role in tailoring topological transport phenomena like the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) remains largely unexplored. Here, we control the sign of polarity-induced charge in SrIrO3-LaCoO3 interfaces by independently engineering the layer stacking sequence and the atomic termination. In-situ angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy directly confirms the sign reversal of the induced charge in SrIrO3 through the contrasting electronic band shifts between different interfacial configurations. Magneto-transport measurements across a systematic matrix of four distinct heterostructures reveal that the AHE can be cleanly toggled on and off: it emerges exclusively under electron-doped conditions, while remaining suppressed for hole-doped SrIrO3. Our results establish that this response originates from an intrinsic, Berry-curvature-driven mechanism governed by polarity-controlled band filling of SrIrO3. These findings shift interfacial polarity from a passive structural consequence to an active design variable for engineering topological quantum states in oxide heterostructures.

item.title: [9] Contrasting fate of holes introduced by Fe or In in kagome metal CoSn
item.description:
Last authors: Victor Bal\'edent, Fran\c{c}ois Bertran

Authors: V\'eronique Brouet, Laure Thomarat, Patrick Le F\`evre, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: title strong match: kagome metal

Tags: #ARPES #angle-resolvedphotoemission #photoemission #kagome #flatband

Abstract: CoSn is a kagome metal with well-defined flat bands 0.2 eV below the Fermi level EF. Moving them across EF would offer a rare opportunity to investigate their impact on electronic properties. Using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and X-ray absorption at the Co K-edge, we examine two routes to introduce holes in this compound, through Co/Fe or Sn/In substitutions. Substituting In for Sn produces an almost rigid upward shift of the bands toward EF, as expected for hole doping, whereas substituting Fe for Co leads to an unexpected downward shift. Density functional theory calculations reproduce these opposite trends and trace the unusual behavior of Fe to its local magnetic moment. The moment keeps the hole on the Fe impurity and imposes an attractive electrostatic potential on neighboring Co atoms. Overall, both substitutions bring weakly dispersing states close to EF, the flat bands of the Co kagome lattice upon In substitution and partly localized states around magnetic Fe impurities upon Fe substitution.

item.title: [9] Symmetry-guided catalogue of chiral phonon materials (Nat. Phys.)
item.description:
Last authors: Ming Shi, Yuanfeng Xu

Authors: Yue Yang, Zhenyu Xiao, Yu Mao, et al.

Published as: Nat. Phys. DOI

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: author whitelist: Ming Shi

Tags: #phonon

Abstract: Chiral phonons---circularly polarized lattice vibrations with angular momentum---have become a key frontier in quantum materials. They offer ways to control heat and information through their coupling to electronic spin, orbital, and valley degrees of freedom. We present a symmetry-based framework that classifies phonon chirality across all crystallographic space groups. Our approach, built on symmetry representations of phonon angular momentum in reciprocal space, identifies three phononic material classes, namely, crystals with no chirality, chiral crystals with conventional s-wave helicity, and a group of achiral crystals hosting exotic higher-order helicities such as d, g, and i waves. Through high-throughput computation, we shortlist the most promising material candidates for experimental investigation. These results are compiled into the open-access Chiral Phonon Materials Database, which enables screening for materials with the desired chiral phonon properties. Our work establishes both the theoretical framework and the material platform required to exploit the properties of chiral phonons for next-generation thermal management and quantum technologies.

item.title: [9] Anomalous Low-temperature Magnetotransport in Kagome Metal CsCr3Sb5 under Pressure (Phys. Rev. Mater.)
item.description:
Last authors: Zhiwei Wang, Swee K. Goh

Authors: Zikai Zhou, Wenyan Wang, Deng Hu, et al.

Published as: Phys. Rev. Mater. DOI

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: title strong match: kagome metal

Tags: #kagome #superconduct #correlated #transport

Abstract: As a unique kagome superconductor displaying clear signatures of strong electronic correlations, CsCr$_3$Sb$_5$ has drawn much attention. Its rich temperature-pressure phase diagram features intertwined orders including pressure-induced superconductivity and two density-wave-like phases, making it an outstanding platform to explore the complex coexistence and competition of multiple quantum orders. At around 30 K, which we designate as $T_3$, a possible anomaly manifesting as a hump in the resistivity has been observed, yet its nature remains largely unexplored due to limited supporting evidence from other probes. Here, we conducted systematic magnetotransport experiments under hydrostatic pressure to investigate the nature of this anomaly. Our results reveal an abundance of intriguing magnetotransport signatures below $T_3$, including a non-trivial temperature dependence of the Hall coefficient, multi-band characteristics, and pressure-enhanced anomalous-Hall-like effect. These signatures bear resemblance to those observed in many other correlated materials with distinct origins. These findings suggest the possibility of an additional electronic order in CsCr$_3$Sb$_5$, calling for further detailed investigations.
